subject: Discovery: Reserved GPU planning — Alethia assessment
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@alethia.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & suggested reserved-GPU playbook — Alethia

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the whole team has a single source-of-truth and we can move to a pilot decision quickly.

Pain points you shared:
- Production variability: inference traffic for embeddings + ranking swings wildly (baseline 1.5k TPS; marketing blasts push to ~5k TPS peaks).
- Cost unpredictability on current cloud setup and long cold-start times for scaled replicas.
- Need for data isolation and auditability for PII-sensitive user profiles.

Goals you articulated:
- Stable p95 latency for generation/reranking at <= 120 ms under baseline load.
- Predictable monthly unit costs with headroom for 2x peak bursts.
- Dedicated environment for model inference with VPC isolation + KMS integration.

Notes on current stack (from your description):
- Fronting layer: Node.js microservice on GCP (GKE) calling a mixture of managed endpoints and self-hosted containers.
- Models: mix of open Llama-family for retrieval-augmented generation and a fine-tuned reranker.
- Observability: Datadog for infra, but limited per-token latency/cost breakdowns today.

Redwood Dedicated fit (initial assessment):
- Reserved GPU pools with isolation will address your security/throughput needs.
- Autoscaling + burst capacity can be configured to hold baseline capacity at ~1.8k TPS and allow controlled bursts to ~5k TPS for short windows.
- KV/prefix caching and continuous batching can reduce unit cost for embeddings-heavy workloads.

Next steps I recommend (with owners & ETA):
1) I will send an initial reserved-pool playbook + capacity worksheet (attached) for your ops team to review — Hannah (today EOD).
2) Marcus to follow up with a short technical checklist to validate network/KMS constraints — Marcus (morning Wed).
3) Alethia to confirm two representative workload traces (7 days preferred) and a target latency SLO — Emily (by Fri 5/14).
4) Align on pilot window and acceptance criteria (cost/latency/regression) and schedule kickoff — all (next week).

Attachments included: reserved-playbook-v0.1.pdf (playbook draft), capacity-estimate-alethia.xlsx (rough numbers).

If any of this is incorrect or missing, flag it — otherwise, I’ll queue the pilot materials and Marcus will reach out with the technical checklist.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserved-playbook-v0.1.pdf (PDF, 180 KB)]

From: Emily Zhao <emily@alethia.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@alethia.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & suggested reserved-GPU playbook — Alethia

Thanks Hannah — this is great and matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline is closer to 1.2k TPS on weekdays and 1.8k on weekends; the 5k peaks happen during promotional pushes and last ~20–30 minutes.
- Our current SLA target is 100 ms p95 for reranking, 200 ms p95 for generation. If Redwood can give predictable economics for that, we’re very interested.
- On isolation: we need VPC + customer-managed KMS and the ability to encrypt cached embeddings at rest.

We’ll share workload traces by Thursday EOD — ops will extract anonymized logs. Also looping in our infra lead (ops@alethia.ai) for the network/KMS check.

Quick ask: can Marcus include a short checklist for firewall rules / egress controls? That will help our infra team evaluate faster.

Emily
Emily Zhao
Director, Product 
Alethia Technologies

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 3:10 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the time today...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: ops@alethia.ai, Emily Zhao <emily@alethia.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved-pool technical checklist for Alethia (brief)

Hi team — following Hannah’s recap, here are the concrete technical items we’ll need to validate before a reserved-pool pilot: 

1) Network & routing
- Public egress allowed from Redwood private worker subnets? (yes/no)
- Firewall ports: outbound 443 to api.redwood.com and to our artifact repo (S3 endpoints)
- Private peering or VPN requirements (describe)

2) KMS / key management
- Will Alethia provide a customer-managed KMS key (Y/N) and key ARN?
- Requirement for HSM-backed keys stated? (Y/N)

3) Data handling
- Which datasets must be redacted before sending to Redwood? (list)
- Retention window required for KV/prefix caches

4) Capacity details
- Provide 7-day trace (min), sample QPS, burst profile (we want timeseries + 95/99 percentiles)
- Preferred GPU types and any soft constraints on quantization/latency tradeoffs

I’ve attached a one-page checklist and a short worksheet to capture the above (see attachments). If you prefer, I can hop on a 20-minute tech sync to walk through.

Regards,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity-estimate-alethia.xlsx (XLSX, 45 KB)]

Perfect — thanks Emily & ops. Next sensible step:

- Emily/ops: share anonymized 7-day traces + confirm KMS approach (customer-managed preferred) by Thursday EOD.
- Marcus: I’ll let you own the tech sync if Alethia wants it; propose Thu 5/13 10:00am PT (I’ll send a calendar hold).

If we get the traces and KMS confirmation on Thu, we can aim to have a 2-week pilot ready the week of 5/24 with a small reserved pool sized for baseline + measured burst.

Calendar invite: https://cal.com/hannah/30?c=alethia-pilot

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
